section_1.title: The Mystery of the Slice
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a right circular cone being intersected by a plane. While we know these intersections create ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas, the 'why' is often missing. This section defines the goal: proving that the intersection curve is an ellipse using a beautiful 3D construction.
section_1.example: A wizard character, 'Mathemagician Max', uses a laser-thin sword to slice through a glowing ice-cream cone at an angle, revealing a perfect oval (ellipse) glowing on the surface.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The 'Equal Tangent' Rule
section_2.content: Establish a critical geometric foundation: From any single point outside a sphere, the lengths of the two tangent segments to the sphere are exactly equal. This is the 'secret weapon' for the upcoming proof.
section_2.example: An animation of a squirrel standing at a point P outside a giant snowball. It holds two straight sticks that just touch the snowball at points A and B. A measuring tape shows that PA = PB regardless of where the squirrel moves the sticks.

section_3.title: Summoning the Dandelin Spheres
section_3.content: Introduce the construction: Place two spheres (Dandelin Spheres) inside the cone. One is small and sits above the intersecting plane; the other is large and sits below. Each sphere must be tangent to the cone (along a circle) and tangent to the plane (at a single point). Let these points of tangency on the plane be F1 and F2.
section_3.example: Visualize two soap bubbles inflating inside a funnel until they are snugly 'wedged' between the funnel walls and a tilted glass sheet. The points where the bubbles touch the glass are highlighted as 'Magic Foci' (F1 and F2).

section_4.title: The Step-by-Step Proof
section_4.content: Pick an arbitrary point P on the intersection curve. Using the tangent rule from Section 2, show that the distance from P to F1 is equal to the distance from P to the upper circle of tangency on the cone. Similarly, PF2 equals the distance to the lower circle. Therefore, PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance between the two circles, which is constant.
section_4.example: A glowing string is drawn from F1 to P and then to F2. As P slides around the edge of the slice, the animation shows the segments mapping onto the side of the cone, maintaining a constant total length, satisfying the definition of an ellipse.

section_5.title: Generalization and Real-World Echoes
section_5.content: Explain that this logic isn't just for ellipses. By changing the angle of the plane, Dandelin spheres can also define parabolas and hyperbolas. Conclude with why this matters: it links 3D spatial geometry with 2D coordinate geometry.
section_5.example: A 'Section-O-Matic' machine shifts the plane's angle. We see the Dandelin spheres resize and shift to stay tangent, showing how the math holds true for a satellite's orbit (ellipse) or a comet's flyby (hyperbola).

outline.title: The Mystery of the Slice
outline.content: Introduce the concept of a right circular cone being intersected by a plane. While we know these intersections create ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas, the 'why' is often missing. This section defines the goal: proving that the intersection curve is an ellipse using a beautiful 3D construction.
outline.example: A wizard character, 'Mathemagician Max', uses a laser-thin sword to slice through a glowing ice-cream cone at an angle, revealing a perfect oval (ellipse) glowing on the surface.

storyboard.title: The Mystery of the Slice
lecture_lines: A cone's intersection with a plane creates beautiful curves.
Slanted cuts specifically produce a shape called an ellipse.
We will prove why this geometry works using spheres.
animations: Show a 3D cone (white #FFFFFF) and a tilted plane (blue #1E90FF).
Highlight the intersection curve (ellipse) in bright yellow #FFFF00.
Rotate the view to show the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00) from a top-down perspective.
Pulse the yellow #FFFF00 ellipse to emphasize its shape.
Zoom out to show the cone (white #FFFFFF) and plane (blue #1E90FF) again.

outline.title: Prerequisite: The 'Equal Tangent' Rule
outline.content: Establish a critical geometric foundation: From any single point outside a sphere, the lengths of the two tangent segments to the sphere are exactly equal. This is the 'secret weapon' for the upcoming proof.
outline.example: An animation of a squirrel standing at a point P outside a giant snowball. It holds two straight sticks that just touch the snowball at points A and B. A measuring tape shows that PA = PB regardless of where the squirrel moves the sticks.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The 'Equal Tangent' Rule
lecture_lines: Consider a point outside a sphere.
Two tangent segments drawn to the sphere are equal.
This simple rule is key to our upcoming proof.
animations: Display a sphere (silver #C0C0C0) and a point P (red #FF0000) outside it.
Draw two tangent lines from P (red #FF0000) to points A and B (green #00FF00) on the sphere.
Show labels "PA" and "PB" and highlight segments PA and PB (yellow #FFFF00) to show equality.

outline.title: Summoning the Dandelin Spheres
outline.content: Introduce the construction: Place two spheres (Dandelin Spheres) inside the cone. One is small and sits above the intersecting plane; the other is large and sits below. Each sphere must be tangent to the cone (along a circle) and tangent to the plane (at a single point). Let these points of tangency on the plane be F1 and F2.

These points of contact are called the Dandelin foci.

outline.title: The Step-by-Step Proof
outline.content: Pick an arbitrary point P on the intersection curve. Using the tangent rule from Section 2, show that the distance from P to F1 is equal to the distance from P to the upper circle of tangency on the cone. Similarly, PF2 equals the distance to the lower circle. Therefore, PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance between the two circles, which is constant.
outline.example: A glowing string is drawn from F1 to P and then to F2. As P slides around the edge of the slice, the animation shows the segments mapping onto the side of the cone, maintaining a constant total length, satisfying the definition of an ellipse.

storyboard.title: The Step-by-Step Proof
lecture_lines: Pick any point P on the intersection curve.
Connect P to both Dandelin foci, F1 and F2.
PF1 and PF2 equal the distances to the circles.
The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance.
This constant sum defines the shape as an ellipse.
animations: Highlight point P (green #00FF00) on the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00).
Draw lines PF1 (red #FF0000) and a line from P to the upper circle (cyan #00FFFF); show they match.
Draw lines PF2 (red #FF0000) and a line from P to the lower circle (magenta #FF00FF); show they match.
Highlight the slant segment (orange #FFA500) between the two circles on the cone's surface.
Move P (green #00FF00) along the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00) while keeping the sum PF1+PF2 constant.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Mystery of the Slice"
        lines = [
            "A cone's intersection with a plane creates beautiful curves.",
            "Slanted cuts specifically produce a shape called an ellipse.",
            "We will prove why this geometry works using spheres."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_CONE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_PLANE = "#1E90FF"
        COLOR_ELLIPSE = "#FFFF00"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a 3D-looking cone (2D triangle with curved top) and a tilted plane.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Cone (vertex at bottom)
        cone_body = Polygon(
            [0, -1.5, 0], [1.2, 1.5, 0], [-1.2, 1.5, 0],
            color=COLOR_CONE, fill_opacity=0.2
        )
        cone_top = Ellipse(width=2.4, height=0.6, color=COLOR_CONE).move_to([0, 1.5, 0])
        cone = VGroup(cone_body, cone_top)
        
        # Tilted Plane (represented as a thin rectangle/parallelogram)
        plane = Polygon(
            [-1.5, 0.5, 0], [1.5, -0.5, 0], [1.5, -0.7, 0], [-1.5, 0.3, 0],
            color=COLOR_PLANE, fill_opacity=0.5
        )
        # Shift plane to intersect cone
        plane.move_to([0, 0.2, 0])
        
        visuals_1 = VGroup(cone, plane)
        self.place_in_area(visuals_1, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the intersection curve (ellipse) in bright yellow.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_ELLIPSE)
        
        # Ellipse at intersection
        # It should be tilted and centered where plane meets cone
        intersection_ellipse = Ellipse(
            width=1.8, height=0.5, color=COLOR_ELLIPSE, stroke_width=6
        )
        intersection_ellipse.rotate(-15 * DEGREES) # Match plane tilt roughly
        intersection_ellipse.move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(intersection_ellipse), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Rotate the view to show the ellipse from a top-down perspective, pulse it, then zoom out.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_ELLIPSE) # Using yellow for consistency with ellipse focus
        
        # Group everything for the "rotation" simulation
        full_scene = VGroup(cone, plane, intersection_ellipse)
        
        # Simulation of "top-down view": Transform the whole scene to look like a circle
        # but the prompt says "Rotate the view", we'll simulate this by flattening the cone and making ellipse a circle.
        top_down_ellipse = Ellipse(width=2.0, height=2.0, color=COLOR_ELLIPSE, stroke_width=6)
        top_down_ellipse.move_to(intersection_ellipse.get_center())
        
        # We'll fade out the cone and plane to focus on the ellipse for the "top-down" part
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cone),
            FadeOut(plane),
            Transform(intersection_ellipse, top_down_ellipse),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Pulse the yellow ellipse
        self.play(
            intersection_ellipse.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            intersection_ellipse.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Zoom out/Return to perspective
        # To "Zoom out", we bring back the cone and plane and transform the ellipse back
        original_ellipse = Ellipse(
            width=1.8, height=0.5, color=COLOR_ELLIPSE, stroke_width=6
        ).rotate(-15 * DEGREES).move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(cone),
            FadeIn(plane),
            Transform(intersection_ellipse, original_ellipse),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset colors for final state
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)

        self.play(Create(intersection_ellipse), run_time=1)

            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            intersection_ellipse.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Zoom out/Return to perspective

            width=1.8, height=0.5, color=COLOR_ELLIPSE, stroke_width=6
        ).rotate(-15 * DEGREES).move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(cone),
            FadeIn(plane),
            Transform(intersection_ellipse, original_ellipse),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset colors for final state
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=1

            c = np.cos(theta)

            r1 = (ay - ys1) * s

            # Sphere 2 (Bottom/Inside)
            if abs(s - c) < 0.05:

        # Transition back to ellipse to show spheres clearly

        # Tracker for the angle of the slicing plane
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0.3)
        
        # Diagram setup (2D side-view representation)
        diagram_center = self.grid["D4"]
        scale = 0.7
        
        # Cone lines relative to diagram_center
        rel_apex = np.array([0, 1.5 * scale, 0])
        cone = VGroup(
            Line(diagram_center + rel_apex, diagram_center + np.array([-1.5*scale, -1.5*scale, 0]), color=CONE_COLOR),
            Line(diagram_center + rel_apex, diagram_center + np.array([1.5*scale, -1.5*scale, 0]), color=CONE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Rotating Plane line
        rel_pivot = np.array([0, -0.5 * scale, 0])
        plane = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            diagram_center + rel_pivot + rotate_vector(LEFT * 1.5 * scale, angle_tracker.get_value()),
            diagram_center + rel_pivot + rotate_vector(RIGHT * 1.5 * scale, angle_tracker.get_value()),
            color=PLANE_COLOR, stroke_width=4
        ))

        # Dynamic label for the conic type based on angle
        def get_type_text():
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            wall_angle = np.arctan(2.0) # Angle of the cone wall
            if abs(theta) < wall_angle - 0.1: return "ELLIPSE"
            if abs(theta) < wall_angle + 0.1: return "PARABOLA"
            return "HYPERBOLA"
            
        type_label = always_redraw(lambda: Text(
            get_type_text(), font_size=18, color=CONIC_COLOR
        ).next_to(plane, UP, buff=0.1))

        # Dandelin Spheres (circles in side view)
        sphere1 = Circle(color=SPHERE_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        sphere2 = Circle(color=SPHERE_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        spheres = VGroup(sphere1, sphere2)
        
        def update_spheres(m):
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            m_cone = 2.0 # slope of the cone wall (3 height / 1.5 half-width)
            ay = 1.5 * scale # apex y
            py = -0.5 * scale # pivot y
            
            s = np.sin(np.arctan(1/m_cone))
            c = np.cos(theta)
            
            # Sphere 1 (Top/Inside)
            # Center (0, ys1), radius r1
            ys1 = (ay * s + py * c) / (s + c)
            r1 = (ay - ys1) * s
            if 0 < r1 < 2:
                sphere1.set_width(max(0.01, 2*r1)).move_to(diagram_center + np.array([0, ys1, 0])).set_opacity(0.6)
            else:
                sphere1.set_opacity(0)
                
            # Sphere 2 (Bottom/Inside)
            if abs(s - c) < 0.05:
                sphere2.set_opacity(0)
            else:
                ys2 = (ay * s - py * c) / (s - c)
                r2 = abs((ay - ys2) * s)
                if 0 < r2 < 2.2:
                    sphere2.set_width(max(0.01, 2*r2)).move_to(diagram_center + np.array([0, ys2, 0])).set_opacity(0.6)
                else:
                    sphere2.set_opacity(0)
        
        spheres.add_updater(update_spheres)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Changing the plane's angle creates parabolas and hyperbolas."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(PLANE_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(cone))
        self.play(Create(plane), Write(type_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Show Parabola angle
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(1.107), run_time=2) 
        self.wait(1)
        # Show Hyperbola angle
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4), run_time=2) 
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Dandelin spheres reveal the logic behind all conic sections."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(SPHERE_COLOR))
        # Transition back to ellipse to show spheres clearly
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(0.4), run_time=1.5) 
        self.play(FadeIn(spheres))
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Watch spheres adjust as plane tilts through types
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(1.3), run_time=3.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Geometry bridges the gap between 3D space and 2D curves."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CONIC_COLOR))
        
        # Conclude with glowing curves representation
        ellipse_c = Ellipse(width=1.5, height=1.0, color=CONIC_COLOR).set_stroke(width=5)
        parabola_c = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5*x**2 - 0.5, x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color=CONIC_COLOR).set_stroke(width=5)
        hyperbola_c = VGroup(
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.5) - 0.5, x_range=[-1.2, 1.2], color=CONIC_COLOR),
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: -np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.5) + 0.5, x_range=[-1.2, 1.2], color=CONIC_COLOR)
        ).set_stroke(width=5)
        
        # Prepare curves at grid position
        self.place_at_grid(ellipse_c, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(parabola_c, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_c, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Transition from diagram to curves
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cone), FadeOut(spheres), FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(type_label)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(ellipse_c))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(ellipse_c, parabola_c))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(parabola_c, hyperbola_c))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Step-by-Step Proof", [
            "Pick any point P on the intersection curve.",
            "Connect P to both Dandelin foci, F1 and F2.",
            "PF1 and PF2 equal the distances to the circles.",
            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance.",
            "This constant sum defines the shape as an ellipse."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight point P (green #00FF00) on the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00).
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.6, height=2.2, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, "B2", "E5")
        
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(PI / 3)
        
        p_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00", z_index=10)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(ellipse.point_at_angle(t_tracker.get_value())))
        
        p_label = Text("P", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UR, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.play(FadeIn(p_dot), Write(p_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Connect P to both Dandelin foci, F1 and F2.
        # Foci: c^2 = a^2 - b^2. a = 1.8, b = 1.1. c = sqrt(3.24 - 1.21) = sqrt(2.03) approx 1.425
        c_val = np.sqrt((1.8)**2 - (1.1)**2)
        f1_pos = ellipse.get_center() + LEFT * c_val
        f2_pos = ellipse.get_center() + RIGHT * c_val
        
        f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color="#FF0000")
        f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color="#FF0000")
        f1_text = Text("F1", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(f1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        f2_text = Text("F2", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(f2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        line_pf1 = Line(color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        line_pf1.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([f1.get_center(), p_dot.get_center()]))
        
        line_pf2 = Line(color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        line_pf2.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([f2.get_center(), p_dot.get_center()]))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(FadeIn(f1), FadeIn(f2), Write(f1_text), Write(f2_text))
        self.play(Create(line_pf1), Create(line_pf2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # PF1 and PF2 equal the distances to the circles.
        # Draw circles as dashed lines for context
        circle_top_y = ellipse.get_center()[1] + 1.8
        circle_bot_y = ellipse.get_center()[1] - 1.8
        
        c1_ref = DashedLine(self.grid['A2'], self.grid['A5'], color=GRAY).set_y(circle_top_y)
        c2_ref = DashedLine(self.grid['F2'], self.grid['F5'], color=GRAY).set_y(circle_bot_y)
        
        # Generator segments: In 2D view, these are segments from P to the circle lines.
        # We align them such that PF1 = P-C1 and PF2 = P-C2 for the start angle.
        # For t=PI/3: PF1 = a + c*cos(PI/3) = 1.8 + 1.425*0.5 = 2.5125
        # PF2 = a - c*cos(PI/3) = 1.8 - 0.7125 = 1.0875
        
        line_p_c1 = Line(color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        line_p_c1.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            p_dot.get_center(), 
            p_dot.get_center() + UP * (1.8 + 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value()))
        ]))
        
        line_p_c2 = Line(color="#FF00FF", stroke_width=4)
        line_p_c2.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            p_dot.get_center(), 
            p_dot.get_center() + DOWN * (1.8 - 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value()))
        ]))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(c1_ref), Create(c2_ref))
        self.play(Create(line_p_c1), Create(line_p_c2))
        
        # Show match
        self.play(Indicate(line_pf1), Indicate(line_p_c1, color="#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(line_pf2), Indicate(line_p_c2, color="#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance.
        # Highlight the slant segment (orange #FFA500) between the two circles.
        # Total distance = (y_p + d1) - (y_p - d2) = d1 + d2 = PF1 + PF2 = 2a = 3.6
        slant_seg = Line(color="#FFA500", stroke_width=8, z_index=-1)
        slant_seg.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            p_dot.get_center() + UP * (1.8 + 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value())),
            p_dot.get_center() + DOWN * (1.8 - 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value()))
        ]))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.play(FadeIn(slant_seg))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This constant sum defines the shape as an ellipse.
        # Move P (green #00FF00) along the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00).
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Move P full circle
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI + PI / 3), run_time=6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Mystery of the Slice
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a right circular cone being intersected by a plane. While we know these intersections create ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas, the 'why' is often missing. This section defines the goal: proving that the intersection curve is an ellipse using a beautiful 3D construction.
section_1.example: A wizard character, 'Mathemagician Max', uses a laser-thin sword to slice through a glowing ice-cream cone at an angle, revealing a perfect oval (ellipse) glowing on the surface.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The 'Equal Tangent' Rule
section_2.content: Establish a critical geometric foundation: From any single point outside a sphere, the lengths of the two tangent segments to the sphere are exactly equal. This is the 'secret weapon' for the upcoming proof.
section_2.example: An animation of a squirrel standing at a point P outside a giant snowball. It holds two straight sticks that just touch the snowball at points A and B. A measuring tape shows that PA = PB regardless of where the squirrel moves the sticks.

section_3.title: Summoning the Dandelin Spheres
section_3.content: Introduce the construction: Place two spheres (Dandelin Spheres) inside the cone. One is small and sits above the intersecting plane; the other is large and sits below. Each sphere must be tangent to the cone (along a circle) and tangent to the plane (at a single point). Let these points of tangency on the plane be F1 and F2.
section_3.example: Visualize two soap bubbles inflating inside a funnel until they are snugly 'wedged' between the funnel walls and a tilted glass sheet. The points where the bubbles touch the glass are highlighted as 'Magic Foci' (F1 and F2).

section_4.title: The Step-by-Step Proof
section_4.content: Pick an arbitrary point P on the intersection curve. Using the tangent rule from Section 2, show that the distance from P to F1 is equal to the distance from P to the upper circle of tangency on the cone. Similarly, PF2 equals the distance to the lower circle. Therefore, PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance between the two circles, which is constant.
section_4.example: A glowing string is drawn from F1 to P and then to F2. As P slides around the edge of the slice, the animation shows the segments mapping onto the side of the cone, maintaining a constant total length, satisfying the definition of an ellipse.

section_5.title: Generalization and Real-World Echoes
section_5.content: Explain that this logic isn't just for ellipses. By changing the angle of the plane, Dandelin spheres can also define parabolas and hyperbolas. Conclude with why this matters: it links 3D spatial geometry with 2D coordinate geometry.
section_5.example: A 'Section-O-Matic' machine shifts the plane's angle. We see the Dandelin spheres resize and shift to stay tangent, showing how the math holds true for a satellite's orbit (ellipse) or a comet's flyby (hyperbola).

        self.lecture[0].set_color(highlight_color)
        
        # Create a sphere (represented as a Circle with radial gradient for 2D look)
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.2, color=sphere_color, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sphere.set_fill(sphere_color, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, "C2")
        
        point_p = Dot(color=point_color)
        self.place_at_grid(point_p, "C5")
        label_p = MathTex("P", color=point_color).next_to(point_p, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(sphere), FadeIn(point_p), Write(label_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(highlight_color)

        # Calculate tangent points
        center_pos = self.grid["C2"]
        p_pos = self.grid["C5"]
        r = 1.2 # sphere radius
        
        d = np.linalg.norm(p_pos - center_pos)
        alpha = np.arccos(r / d)
        
        # Vector from C to P
        vec_cp = p_pos - center_pos
        angle_cp = np.arctan2(vec_cp[1], vec_cp[0])
        
        # Positions of A and B
        pos_a = center_pos + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp + alpha), np.sin(angle_cp + alpha), 0])
        pos_b = center_pos + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp - alpha), np.sin(angle_cp - alpha), 0])
        
        dot_a = Dot(pos_a, color=tangent_point_color)
        dot_b = Dot(pos_b, color=tangent_point_color)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=tangent_point_color).next_to(dot_a, UP + LEFT, buff=0.1)
        label_b = MathTex("B", color=tangent_point_color).next_to(dot_b, DOWN + LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        line_pa = Line(p_pos, pos_a, color=point_color)
        line_pb = Line(p_pos, pos_b, color=point_color)
        
        self.play(
            Create(line_pa), 
            Create(line_pb),
            FadeIn(dot_a),
            FadeIn(dot_b),
            Write(label_a),
            Write(label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(highlight_color)
        
        # Highlight PA and PB in yellow
        rect_pa = line_pa.copy().set_color(highlight_color).set_stroke(width=6)
        rect_pb = line_pb.copy().set_color(highlight_color).set_stroke(width=6)
        
        # Labels for segment lengths
        label_pa_text = MathTex("PA", color=highlight_color).next_to(line_pa, UP, buff=0.2).shift(LEFT*0.3)
        label_pb_text = MathTex("PB", color=highlight_color).next_to(line_pb, DOWN, buff=0.2).shift(LEFT*0.3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Step-by-Step Proof", [
            "Pick any point P on the intersection curve.",
            "Connect P to both Dandelin foci, F1 and F2.",
            "PF1 and PF2 equal the distances to the circles.",
            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance.",
            "This constant sum defines the shape as an ellipse."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight point P (green #00FF00) on the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00).
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.6, height=2.2, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, "B2", "E5")
        
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(PI / 3)
        
        p_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00", z_index=10)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(ellipse.point_at_angle(t_tracker.get_value())))
        
        p_label = Text("P", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UR, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.play(FadeIn(p_dot), Write(p_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Connect P to both Dandelin foci, F1 and F2.
        # Foci: c^2 = a^2 - b^2. a = 1.8, b = 1.1. c = sqrt(3.24 - 1.21) = sqrt(2.03) approx 1.425
        c_val = np.sqrt((1.8)**2 - (1.1)**2)
        f1_pos = ellipse.get_center() + LEFT * c_val
        f2_pos = ellipse.get_center() + RIGHT * c_val
        
        f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color="#FF0000")
        f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color="#FF0000")
        f1_text = Text("F1", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(f1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        f2_text = Text("F2", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(f2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        line_pf1 = Line(color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        line_pf1.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([f1.get_center(), p_dot.get_center()]))
        
        line_pf2 = Line(color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        line_pf2.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([f2.get_center(), p_dot.get_center()]))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(FadeIn(f1), FadeIn(f2), Write(f1_text), Write(f2_text))
        self.play(Create(line_pf1), Create(line_pf2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # PF1 and PF2 equal the distances to the circles.
        # Draw circles as dashed lines for context
        circle_top_y = ellipse.get_center()[1] + 1.8
        circle_bot_y = ellipse.get_center()[1] - 1.8
        
        c1_ref = DashedLine(self.grid['A2'], self.grid['A5'], color=GRAY).set_y(circle_top_y)
        c2_ref = DashedLine(self.grid['F2'], self.grid['F5'], color=GRAY).set_y(circle_bot_y)
        
        # Generator segments: In 2D view, these are segments from P to the circle lines.
        # We align them such that PF1 = P-C1 and PF2 = P-C2 for the start angle.
        # For t=PI/3: PF1 = a + c*cos(PI/3) = 1.8 + 1.425*0.5 = 2.5125
        # PF2 = a - c*cos(PI/3) = 1.8 - 0.7125 = 1.0875
        
        line_p_c1 = Line(color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        line_p_c1.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            p_dot.get_center(), 
            p_dot.get_center() + UP * (1.8 + 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value()))
        ]))
        
        line_p_c2 = Line(color="#FF00FF", stroke_width=4)
        line_p_c2.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            p_dot.get_center(), 
            p_dot.get_center() + DOWN * (1.8 - 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value()))
        ]))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(c1_ref), Create(c2_ref))
        self.play(Create(line_p_c1), Create(line_p_c2))
        
        # Show match
        self.play(Indicate(line_pf1), Indicate(line_p_c1, color="#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(line_pf2), Indicate(line_p_c2, color="#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance.
        # Highlight the slant segment (orange #FFA500) between the two circles.
        # Total distance = (y_p + d1) - (y_p - d2) = d1 + d2 = PF1 + PF2 = 2a = 3.6
        slant_seg = Line(color="#FFA500", stroke_width=8, z_index=-1)
        slant_seg.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            p_dot.get_center() + UP * (1.8 + 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value())),
            p_dot.get_center() + DOWN * (1.8 - 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value()))
        ]))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.play(FadeIn(slant_seg))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This constant sum defines the shape as an ellipse.
        # Move P (green #00FF00) along the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00).
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Move P full circle
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI + PI / 3), run_time=6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout
        lines = [
            "Changing the plane's angle creates parabolas and hyperbolas.",
            "Dandelin spheres reveal the logic behind all conic sections.",
            "Geometry bridges the gap between 3D space and 2D curves."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Generalization and Real-World Echoes", lines)
        
        # Colors based on storyboard requirements
        PLANE_COLOR = "#1E90FF"
        SPHERE_COLOR = "#D3D3D3"
        CONIC_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        CONE_COLOR = "#666666"

        # Tracker for the angle of the slicing plane
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0.3)
        
        # Diagram setup (2D side-view representation)
        diagram_center = self.grid["D4"]
        scale = 0.7
        
        # Cone lines relative to diagram_center
        rel_apex = np.array([0, 1.5 * scale, 0])
        cone = VGroup(
            Line(diagram_center + rel_apex, diagram_center + np.array([-1.5*scale, -1.5*scale, 0]), color=CONE_COLOR),
            Line(diagram_center + rel_apex, diagram_center + np.array([1.5*scale, -1.5*scale, 0]), color=CONE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Rotating Plane line
        rel_pivot = np.array([0, -0.5 * scale, 0])
        plane = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            diagram_center + rel_pivot + rotate_vector(LEFT * 1.5 * scale, angle_tracker.get_value()),
            diagram_center + rel_pivot + rotate_vector(RIGHT * 1.5 * scale, angle_tracker.get_value()),
            color=PLANE_COLOR, stroke_width=4
        ))

        # Dynamic label for the conic type based on angle
        def get_type_text():
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            wall_angle = np.arctan(2.0) # Angle of the cone wall
            if abs(theta) < wall_angle - 0.1: return "ELLIPSE"
            if abs(theta) < wall_angle + 0.1: return "PARABOLA"
            return "HYPERBOLA"
            
        type_label = always_redraw(lambda: Text(
            get_type_text(), font_size=18, color=CONIC_COLOR
        ).next_to(plane, UP, buff=0.1))

        # Dandelin Spheres (circles in side view)
        sphere1 = Circle(color=SPHERE_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        sphere2 = Circle(color=SPHERE_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        spheres = VGroup(sphere1, sphere2)
        
        def update_spheres(m):
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            m_cone = 2.0 # slope of the cone wall (3 height / 1.5 half-width)
            ay = 1.5 * scale # apex y
            py = -0.5 * scale # pivot y
            
            s = np.sin(np.arctan(1/m_cone))
            c = np.cos(theta)
            
            # Sphere 1 (Top/Inside)
            # Center (0, ys1), radius r1
            ys1 = (ay * s + py * c) / (s + c)
            r1 = (ay - ys1) * s
            if 0 < r1 < 2:
                sphere1.set_width(max(0.01, 2*r1)).move_to(diagram_center + np.array([0, ys1, 0])).set_opacity(0.6)
            else:
                sphere1.set_opacity(0)
                
            # Sphere 2 (Bottom/Inside)
            if abs(s - c) < 0.05:
                sphere2.set_opacity(0)
            else:
                ys2 = (ay * s - py * c) / (s - c)
                r2 = abs((ay - ys2) * s)
                if 0 < r2 < 2.2:
                    sphere2.set_width(max(0.01, 2*r2)).move_to(diagram_center + np.array([0, ys2, 0])).set_opacity(0.6)
                else:
                    sphere2.set_opacity(0)
        
        spheres.add_updater(update_spheres)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Changing the plane's angle creates parabolas and hyperbolas."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(PLANE_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(cone))
        self.play(Create(plane), Write(type_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Show Parabola angle
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(1.107), run_time=2) 
        self.wait(1)
        # Show Hyperbola angle
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4), run_time=2) 
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Dandelin spheres reveal the logic behind all conic sections."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(SPHERE_COLOR))
        # Transition back to ellipse to show spheres clearly
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(0.4), run_time=1.5) 
        self.play(FadeIn(spheres))
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Watch spheres adjust as plane tilts through types
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(1.3), run_time=3.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Geometry bridges the gap between 3D space and 2D curves."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CONIC_COLOR))
        
        # Conclude with glowing curves representation
        ellipse_c = Ellipse(width=1.5, height=1.0, color=CONIC_COLOR).set_stroke(width=5)
        parabola_c = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5*x**2 - 0.5, x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color=CONIC_COLOR).set_stroke(width=5)
        hyperbola_c = VGroup(
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.5) - 0.5, x_range=[-1.2, 1.2], color=CONIC_COLOR),
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: -np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.5) + 0.5, x_range=[-1.2, 1.2], color=CONIC_COLOR)
        ).set_stroke(width=5)
        
        # Prepare curves at grid position
        self.place_at_grid(ellipse_c, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(parabola_c, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_c, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Transition from diagram to curves
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cone), FadeOut(spheres), FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(type_label)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(ellipse_c))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(ellipse_c, parabola_c))
        self.wait(1)

outline.title: The Mystery of the Slice
outline.content: Introduce the concept of a right circular cone being intersected by a plane. While we know these intersections create ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas, the 'why' is often missing. This section defines the goal: proving that the intersection curve is an ellipse using a beautiful 3D construction.
outline.example: A wizard character, 'Mathemagician Max', uses a laser-thin sword to slice through a glowing ice-cream cone at an angle, revealing a perfect oval (ellipse) glowing on the surface.

storyboard.title: The Mystery of the Slice
lecture_lines: A cone's intersection with a plane creates beautiful curves.
Slanted cuts specifically produce a shape called an ellipse.
We will prove why this geometry works using spheres.
animations: Show a 3D cone (white #FFFFFF) and a tilted plane (blue #1E90FF).
Highlight the intersection curve (ellipse) in bright yellow #FFFF00.
Rotate the view to show the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00) from a top-down perspective.
Pulse the yellow #FFFF00 ellipse to emphasize its shape.
Zoom out to show the cone (white #FFFFFF) and plane (blue #1E90FF) again.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Mystery of the Slice"
        lines = [
            "A cone's intersection with a plane creates beautiful curves.",
            "Slanted cuts specifically produce a shape called an ellipse.",
            "We will prove why this geometry works using spheres."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_CONE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_PLANE = "#1E90FF"
        COLOR_ELLIPSE = "#FFFF00"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a 3D-looking cone (2D triangle with curved top) and a tilted plane.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Cone (vertex at bottom)
        cone_body = Polygon(
            [0, -1.5, 0], [1.2, 1.5, 0], [-1.2, 1.5, 0],
            color=COLOR_CONE, fill_opacity=0.2
        )
        cone_top = Ellipse(width=2.4, height=0.6, color=COLOR_CONE).move_to([0, 1.5, 0])
        cone = VGroup(cone_body, cone_top)
        
        # Tilted Plane (represented as a thin rectangle/parallelogram)
        plane = Polygon(
            [-1.5, 0.5, 0], [1.5, -0.5, 0], [1.5, -0.7, 0], [-1.5, 0.3, 0],
            color=COLOR_PLANE, fill_opacity=0.5
        )
        # Shift plane to intersect cone
        plane.move_to([0, 0.2, 0])
        
        visuals_1 = VGroup(cone, plane)
        self.place_in_area(visuals_1, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the intersection curve (ellipse) in bright yellow.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_ELLIPSE)
        
        # Ellipse at intersection
        # It should be tilted and centered where plane meets cone
        intersection_ellipse = Ellipse(
            width=1.8, height=0.5, color=COLOR_ELLIPSE, stroke_width=6
        )
        intersection_ellipse.rotate(-15 * DEGREES) # Match plane tilt roughly
        intersection_ellipse.move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(intersection_ellipse), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Rotate the view to show the ellipse from a top-down perspective, pulse it, then zoom out.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_ELLIPSE) # Using yellow for consistency with ellipse focus
        
        # Group everything for the "rotation" simulation
        full_scene = VGroup(cone, plane, intersection_ellipse)
        
        # Simulation of "top-down view": Transform the whole scene to look like a circle
        # but the prompt says "Rotate the view", we'll simulate this by flattening the cone and making ellipse a circle.
        top_down_ellipse = Ellipse(width=2.0, height=2.0, color=COLOR_ELLIPSE, stroke_width=6)
        top_down_ellipse.move_to(intersection_ellipse.get_center())
        
        # We'll fade out the cone and plane to focus on the ellipse for the "top-down" part
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cone),
            FadeOut(plane),
            Transform(intersection_ellipse, top_down_ellipse),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Pulse the yellow ellipse
        self.play(
            intersection_ellipse.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            intersection_ellipse.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Zoom out/Return to perspective
        # To "Zoom out", we bring back the cone and plane and transform the ellipse back
        original_ellipse = Ellipse(
            width=1.8, height=0.5, color=COLOR_ELLIPSE, stroke_width=6
        ).rotate(-15 * DEGREES).move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(cone),
            FadeIn(plane),
            Transform(intersection_ellipse, original_ellipse),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset colors for final state
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout
        lines = [
            "Changing the plane's angle creates parabolas and hyperbolas.",
            "Dandelin spheres reveal the logic behind all conic sections.",
            "Geometry bridges the gap between 3D space and 2D curves."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Generalization and Real-World Echoes", lines)
        
        # Colors based on storyboard requirements
        PLANE_COLOR = "#1E90FF"
        SPHERE_COLOR = "#D3D3D3"
        CONIC_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        CONE_COLOR = "#666666"

        # Tracker for the angle of the slicing plane
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0.3)
        
        # Diagram setup (2D side-view representation)
        diagram_center = self.grid["D4"]
        scale = 0.7
        
        # Cone lines relative to diagram_center
        rel_apex = np.array([0, 1.5 * scale, 0])
        cone = VGroup(
            Line(diagram_center + rel_apex, diagram_center + np.array([-1.5*scale, -1.5*scale, 0]), color=CONE_COLOR),
            Line(diagram_center + rel_apex, diagram_center + np.array([1.5*scale, -1.5*scale, 0]), color=CONE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Rotating Plane line
        rel_pivot = np.array([0, -0.5 * scale, 0])
        plane = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            diagram_center + rel_pivot + rotate_vector(LEFT * 1.5 * scale, angle_tracker.get_value()),
            diagram_center + rel_pivot + rotate_vector(RIGHT * 1.5 * scale, angle_tracker.get_value()),
            color=PLANE_COLOR, stroke_width=4
        ))

        # Dynamic label for the conic type based on angle
        def get_type_text():
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            wall_angle = np.arctan(2.0) # Angle of the cone wall
            if abs(theta) < wall_angle - 0.1: return "ELLIPSE"
            if abs(theta) < wall_angle + 0.1: return "PARABOLA"
            return "HYPERBOLA"
            
        type_label = always_redraw(lambda: Text(
            get_type_text(), font_size=18, color=CONIC_COLOR
        ).next_to(plane, UP, buff=0.1))

        # Dandelin Spheres (circles in side view)
        sphere1 = Circle(color=SPHERE_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        sphere2 = Circle(color=SPHERE_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        spheres = VGroup(sphere1, sphere2)
        
        def update_spheres(m):
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            m_cone = 2.0 # slope of the cone wall (3 height / 1.5 half-width)
            ay = 1.5 * scale # apex y
            py = -0.5 * scale # pivot y
            
            s = np.sin(np.arctan(1/m_cone))
            c = np.cos(theta)
            
            # Sphere 1 (Top/Inside)
            # Center (0, ys1), radius r1
            ys1 = (ay * s + py * c) / (s + c)
            r1 = (ay - ys1) * s
            if 0 < r1 < 2:
                sphere1.set_width(max(0.01, 2*r1)).move_to(diagram_center + np.array([0, ys1, 0])).set_opacity(0.6)
            else:
                sphere1.set_opacity(0)
                
            # Sphere 2 (Bottom/Inside)
            if abs(s - c) < 0.05:
                sphere2.set_opacity(0)
            else:
                ys2 = (ay * s - py * c) / (s - c)
                r2 = abs((ay - ys2) * s)
                if 0 < r2 < 2.2:
                    sphere2.set_width(max(0.01, 2*r2)).move_to(diagram_center + np.array([0, ys2, 0])).set_opacity(0.6)
                else:
                    sphere2.set_opacity(0)
        
        spheres.add_updater(update_spheres)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Changing the plane's angle creates parabolas and hyperbolas."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(PLANE_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(cone))
        self.play(Create(plane), Write(type_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Show Parabola angle
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(1.107), run_time=2) 
        self.wait(1)
        # Show Hyperbola angle
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4), run_time=2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Prerequisite: The 'Equal Tangent' Rule"
        lines = [
            "Consider a point outside a sphere.",
            "Two tangent segments drawn to the sphere are equal.",
            "This simple rule is key to our upcoming proof."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        sphere_color = "#C0C0C0"
        point_color = "#FF0000"
        tangent_point_color = "#00FF00"
        highlight_color = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(highlight_color)
        
        # Create a sphere (represented as a Circle with radial gradient for 2D look)
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.2, color=sphere_color, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sphere.set_fill(sphere_color, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, "C2")
        
        point_p = Dot(color=point_color)
        self.place_at_grid(point_p, "C5")
        label_p = MathTex("P", color=point_color).next_to(point_p, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(sphere), FadeIn(point_p), Write(label_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(highlight_color)

        # Calculate tangent points
        center_pos = self.grid["C2"]
        p_pos = self.grid["C5"]
        r = 1.2 # sphere radius
        
        d = np.linalg.norm(p_pos - center_pos)
        alpha = np.arccos(r / d)
        
        # Vector from C to P
        vec_cp = p_pos - center_pos
        angle_cp = np.arctan2(vec_cp[1], vec_cp[0])
        
        # Positions of A and B
        pos_a = center_pos + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp + alpha), np.sin(angle_cp + alpha), 0])
        pos_b = center_pos + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp - alpha), np.sin(angle_cp - alpha), 0])
        
        dot_a = Dot(pos_a, color=tangent_point_color)
        dot_b = Dot(pos_b, color=tangent_point_color)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=tangent_point_color).next_to(dot_a, UP + LEFT, buff=0.1)
        label_b = MathTex("B", color=tangent_point_color).next_to(dot_b, DOWN + LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        line_pa = Line(p_pos, pos_a, color=point_color)
        line_pb = Line(p_pos, pos_b, color=point_color)
        
        self.play(
            Create(line_pa), 
            Create(line_pb),
            FadeIn(dot_a),
            FadeIn(dot_b),
            Write(label_a),
            Write(label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(highlight_color)
        
        # Highlight PA and PB in yellow
        rect_pa = line_pa.copy().set_color(highlight_color).set_stroke(width=6)
        rect_pb = line_pb.copy().set_color(highlight_color).set_stroke(width=6)
        
        # Labels for segment lengths
        label_pa_text = MathTex("PA", color=highlight_color).next_to(line_pa, UP, buff=0.2).shift(LEFT*0.3)
        label_pb_text = MathTex("PB", color=highlight_color).next_to(line_pb, DOWN, buff=0.2).shift(LEFT*0.3)
        
        equality = MathTex("PA = PB", color=highlight_color)
        self.place_at_grid(equality, "E3")

        self.play(
            Create(rect_pa),
            Create(rect_pb),
            Write(label_pa_text),
            Write(label_pb_text)
        )
        self.play(Write(equality))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Step-by-Step Proof
outline.content: Pick an arbitrary point P on the intersection curve. Using the tangent rule from Section 2, show that the distance from P to F1 is equal to the distance from P to the upper circle of tangency on the cone. Similarly, PF2 equals the distance to the lower circle. Therefore, PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance between the two circles, which is constant.
outline.example: A glowing string is drawn from F1 to P and then to F2. As P slides around the edge of the slice, the animation shows the segments mapping onto the side of the cone, maintaining a constant total length, satisfying the definition of an ellipse.

storyboard.title: The Step-by-Step Proof
lecture_lines: Pick any point P on the intersection curve.
Connect P to both Dandelin foci, F1 and F2.
PF1 and PF2 equal the distances to the circles.
The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance.
This constant sum defines the shape as an ellipse.
animations: Highlight point P (green #00FF00) on the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00).
Draw lines PF1 (red #FF0000) and a line from P to the upper circle (cyan #00FFFF); show they match.
Draw lines PF2 (red #FF0000) and a line from P to the lower circle (magenta #FF00FF); show they match.
Highlight the slant segment (orange #FFA500) between the two circles on the cone's surface.
Move P (green #00FF00) along the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00) while keeping the sum PF1+PF2 constant.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.grid = {}

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Step-by-Step Proof", [
            "Pick any point P on the intersection curve.",
            "Connect P to both Dandelin foci, F1 and F2.",
            "PF1 and PF2 equal the distances to the circles.",
            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance.",
            "This constant sum defines the shape as an ellipse."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight point P (green #00FF00) on the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00).
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.6, height=2.2, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, "B2", "E5")
        
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(PI / 3)
        
        p_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00", z_index=10)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(ellipse.point_at_angle(t_tracker.get_value())))
        
        p_label = Text("P", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UR, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.play(FadeIn(p_dot), Write(p_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Connect P to both Dandelin foci, F1 and F2.
        # Foci: c^2 = a^2 - b^2. a = 1.8, b = 1.1. c = sqrt(3.24 - 1.21) = sqrt(2.03) approx 1.425
        c_val = np.sqrt((1.8)**2 - (1.1)**2)
        f1_pos = ellipse.get_center() + LEFT * c_val
        f2_pos = ellipse.get_center() + RIGHT * c_val
        
        f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color="#FF0000")
        f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color="#FF0000")
        f1_text = Text("F1", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(f1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        f2_text = Text("F2", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(f2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        line_pf1 = Line(color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        line_pf1.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([f1.get_center(), p_dot.get_center()]))
        
        line_pf2 = Line(color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        line_pf2.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([f2.get_center(), p_dot.get_center()]))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(FadeIn(f1), FadeIn(f2), Write(f1_text), Write(f2_text))
        self.play(Create(line_pf1), Create(line_pf2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # PF1 and PF2 equal the distances to the circles.
        # Draw circles as dashed lines for context
        circle_top_y = ellipse.get_center()[1] + 1.8
        circle_bot_y = ellipse.get_center()[1] - 1.8
        
        c1_ref = DashedLine(self.grid['A2'], self.grid['A5'], color=GRAY).set_y(circle_top_y)
        c2_ref = DashedLine(self.grid['F2'], self.grid['F5'], color=GRAY).set_y(circle_bot_y)
        
        # Generator segments: In 2D view, these are segments from P to the circle lines.
        # We align them such that PF1 = P-C1 and PF2 = P-C2 for the start angle.
        # For t=PI/3: PF1 = a + c*cos(PI/3) = 1.8 + 1.425*0.5 = 2.5125
        # PF2 = a - c*cos(PI/3) = 1.8 - 0.7125 = 1.0875
        
        line_p_c1 = Line(color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        line_p_c1.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            p_dot.get_center(), 
            p_dot.get_center() + UP * (1.8 + 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value()))
        ]))
        
        line_p_c2 = Line(color="#FF00FF", stroke_width=4)
        line_p_c2.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            p_dot.get_center(), 
            p_dot.get_center() + DOWN * (1.8 - 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value()))
        ]))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(c1_ref), Create(c2_ref))
        self.play(Create(line_p_c1), Create(line_p_c2))
        
        # Show match
        self.play(Indicate(line_pf1), Indicate(line_p_c1, color="#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(line_pf2), Indicate(line_p_c2, color="#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the slant distance.
        # Highlight the slant segment (orange #FFA500) between the two circles.
        # Total distance = (y_p + d1) - (y_p - d2) = d1 + d2 = PF1 + PF2 = 2a = 3.6
        slant_seg = Line(color="#FFA500", stroke_width=8, z_index=-1)
        slant_seg.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            p_dot.get_center() + UP * (1.8 + 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value())),
            p_dot.get_center() + DOWN * (1.8 - 1.425 * np.cos(t_tracker.get_value()))
        ]))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.play(FadeIn(slant_seg))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This constant sum defines the shape as an ellipse.
        # Move P (green #00FF00) along the ellipse (yellow #FFFF00).
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Move P full circle
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI + PI / 3), run_time=6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Summoning the Dandelin Spheres
outline.content: Introduce the construction: Place two spheres (Dandelin Spheres) inside the cone. One is small and sits above the intersecting plane; the other is large and sits below. Each sphere must be tangent to the cone (along a circle) and tangent to the plane (at a single point). Let these points of tangency on the plane be F1 and F2.
outline.example: Visualize two soap bubbles inflating inside a funnel until they are snugly 'wedged' between the funnel walls and a tilted glass sheet. The points where the bubbles touch the glass are highlighted as 'Magic Foci' (F1 and F2).

lecture_lines: Place a small sphere above the intersecting plane.
Place a larger sphere below the plane.
Both spheres touch the cone along horizontal circles.
Each sphere also touches the plane at one point.
These points of contact are called the Dandelin foci.

Highlight tangency points F1 and F2 (red #FF0000) on the plane (blue #1E90FF).
Add labels "F1" and "F2" in red #FF0000 near the contact points on the plane.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summoning the Dandelin Spheres", [
            "Place a small sphere above the intersecting plane.",
            "Place a larger sphere below the plane.",
            "Both spheres touch the cone along horizontal circles.",
            "Each sphere also touches the plane at one point.",
            "These points of contact are called the Dandelin foci."
        ])

        # Cone (Cross-section V-shape)
        cone_v = np.array([0, 2.5, 0])
        cone_l = np.array([-2.0, -3, 0])
        cone_r = np.array([2.0, -3, 0])

        # Contact Circles (Dashed horizontal lines where sphere touches cone sides)
        contact_s = DashedLine(np.array([-0.5, 1.4, 0]), np.array([0.5, 1.4, 0]), color=WHITE)

        self.play(Create(cone), Create(plane_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_s))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#D3D3D3"))
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_l))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(Create(contact_s), Create(contact_l))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(FadeIn(f1), FadeIn(f2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(Write(f1_label), Write(f2_label))

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The 'Equal Tangent' Rule"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Consider a point outside a sphere.",
            "Two tangent segments drawn to the sphere are equal.",
            "This simple rule is key to our upcoming proof."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        sphere_color = "#C0C0C0"
        point_color = "#FF0000"
        tangent_point_color = "#00FF00"
        highlight_color = "#FFFF00"
        
        # Grid positions for clarity
        sphere_center_pos = self.grid["C2"]
        p_pos = self.grid["C4"] # As per Issue 25

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(highlight_color)
        
        # Create a sphere (Circle with gradient-like fill)
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.2, color=sphere_color, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sphere.set_fill(sphere_color, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, "C2", scale_factor=1.3) # As per Issue 25
        
        # Point P at C4
        point_p = Dot(p_pos, color=point_color)
        label_p = MathTex("P", color=point_color).next_to(point_p, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(sphere), FadeIn(point_p), Write(label_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(highlight_color)

        # Geometry calculations for tangent points
        r = 1.2 * 1.3 # Effective radius after scaling
        d = np.linalg.norm(p_pos - sphere_center_pos)
        
        # Angle from center to point P
        vec_cp = p_pos - sphere_center_pos
        angle_cp = np.arctan2(vec_cp[1], vec_cp[0])
        
        # Tangent angle: alpha is the angle between CP and CA (or CB)
        # cos(alpha) = r / d
        alpha = np.arccos(r / d)
        
        # Tangent points A and B
        pos_a = sphere_center_pos + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp + alpha), np.sin(angle_cp + alpha), 0])
        pos_b = sphere_center_pos + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp - alpha), np.sin(angle_cp - alpha), 0])
        
        dot_a = Dot(pos_a, color=tangent_point_color)
        dot_b = Dot(pos_b, color=tangent_point_color)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=tangent_point_color).next_to(dot_a, UP + LEFT, buff=0.1)
        label_b = MathTex("B", color=tangent_point_color).next_to(dot_b, DOWN + LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        line_pa = Line(p_pos, pos_a, color=point_color)
        line_pb = Line(p_pos, pos_b, color=point_color)
        
        self.play(
            Create(line_pa), 
            Create(line_pb),
            FadeIn(dot_a),
            FadeIn(dot_b),
            Write(label_a),
            Write(label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(highlight_color)
        
        # Highlight PA and PB segments (yellow)
        highlight_pa = Line(p_pos, pos_a, color=highlight_color, stroke_width=6)
        highlight_pb = Line(p_pos, pos_b, color=highlight_color, stroke_width=6)
        
        # Labels for the segments PA and PB
        label_pa_segment = MathTex("PA", color=highlight_color).scale(0.8)
        label_pa_segment.move_to(line_pa.get_center() + UP * 0.3 + LEFT * 0.1)
        
        label_pb_segment = MathTex("PB", color=highlight_color).scale(0.8)
        label_pb_segment.move_to(line_pb.get_center() + DOWN * 0.3 + LEFT * 0.1)
        
        # Equality text
        equality = MathTex("PA = PB", color=highlight_color)
        # Position and scale using place_in_area as per Issue 25
        self.place_in_area(equality, "E3", "E4", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(
            Create(highlight_pa),
            Create(highlight_pb),
            Write(label_pa_segment),
            Write(label_pb_segment)
        )
        self.play(Write(equality))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup - reset colors
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)
